surfaces.part: ice floe top (white and cyan ice surface)

answer.evidence: The column scan at x=27 shows a light ice top from rows 6-19 under a 1-row outline at row 5. Row 20 (#6cb4d8) is a front-edge line, followed by a mid-blue front face at rows 21-23 and a dark outline at row 24. The other columns show the same structure shifted by a few rows. The silhouette widens gradually from 2 to 41 px over rows 2-13 and narrows over rows 21-26, which reads as a lumpy slab seen from above. A large top surface sits over a blue front face of about 4 rows, so it reads as three-quarter view. The shape is an irregular blob, so the facing is unclear.

styleAnswer.evidence: The floe has a snow-white cap with speckled highlights, light and mid ice blues on the lumpy body, and a deep blue-tinted base. That is about 5 lightness steps. The outline is a dark blue shade of the adjacent ice, not neutral black, which matches the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, and the snow and ice facets carry dot texture. At 8 visible tones per tile it is on par with the hedge reference (9). It is below the stall (17) and the well (20), but those are far more complex multi-material props. It does not look like a sticker next to the references, so a careful artist would accept it beside them, though it is a little simpler than the richest ones.

surfaces.part: blue front face of the ice

answer.evidence: At x=27 the pale ice top runs rows 6-19, about 14 rows. It is capped by a lighter-blue front-edge line at row 20 (#6cb4d8). Below it is a mid-blue front face (rows 21-23) with a dark outline at row 24. The silhouette widens from 2 px at row 2 to 41 px at rows 13-19, then narrows to 13 px at row 26, which matches a lumpy mass with a large top and a vertical front. The top is much taller than a 1-2 row rim, and the front face is 3+ rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The floe is a single-material blob, closest to the hedge reference, and it holds up against it. It has about 5 lightness steps: white snow highlight, pale ice, light blue, mid blue and a deep blue underside. The snow cap has lumpy clumps and speckle, and the body has facets, so it is not a flat fill. The outline is a darker blue lean of the ice, not neutral black. The measured facts agree: 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, 0% near-flat coverage, and 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge. It is below the multi-material stall (17) and well (20), but those carry more materials, so the comparison is not like for like. Texture is somewhat less varied than the best references, but a careful artist would accept it next to the hedge without it looking thinner or more sticker-like.
